doc.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Sinatra, Shirley Horn and film songs
title: Stan Getz's Voices album and vocal groups
summary: Kirchner describes Getz's mid-60s album Voices, with a Claus Ogerman chorus, and Mandel recalls Blossom Dearie's skill at writing for voices.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: [They both laugh]
Have you heard that record?
No, I haven't.
It’s going to be reissued shortly; it was on an album called, Voices, that was done with a rhythm section with Herbie Hancock and Ron Carter and Grady Tate.
Oh, I’d like to have heard that combination.
And a chorus with Claus Ogerman arrangements.
I’d really like to have heard that, a chorus and Claus plus strings?
No, no strings, just a chorus and rhythm section.
Well if Claus wrote the vocal parts I would’ve liked it.
Yeah it’ll be out in June.
Sounds like a Creed Taylor production.
Definitely. From the mid-60s and as a matter of fact, what the only…
Was it like a Blossom Dearie type chorus?
No its…
‘Cause she was very good at choruses, you remember she had the Blue Reys over in Paris.
Um-hm.
She knew how to write for voices.
Yeah, it was hipper than say a Ray Conniff type concept, or something like that…
Oh, oh, well, you know…
And they did some good tunes, well they did, “Barbara's Theme,” although they mistitled it, “I Want to Live,” but they did that, they did, “Where Flamingos Fly,” the John Benson Brooks tune.
Oh yeah…
“I Didn’t Know What Time it Was.”
The one Gil Evans made such a magnificent record on with Jimmy Knepper.
Yeah.
Yeah.
